chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Yazeed ibn Is'haq, from Harun ibn Hamza al-Ghanawi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the prayer in the ship, so he said: 'If it is heavily laden such that when you stand in it it does not move, then pray standing; and if it is light and rolls, then pray seated.'
ai.seo_question: How should one perform prayer on a ship depending on its stability?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *al-mashiqqa* (hardship) in maritime prayer, prioritizing stability over the standard posture. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on practical adaptability, where the physical state of the vessel dictates the validity of standing (*qiyam*) versus sitting (*qada*), ensuring the prayer remains dignified and focused.
